title: Болельщики Спартака и удар судьбы  (Spartak Fans and a Twist of Fate)

segments.t: In the final scene of the episode, Denis goes to collect his day's pay and discovers a shared passion for Spartak Moscow with Viktor Barinov, leading to a generous parting gesture—and a shocking accident in the rain. Let's listen in Russian.
Завтра я тебе спартаковский бар покажу.
Виктор Петрович, я могу что-нибудь для вас сделать напоследок?
Now let's walk through the Russian dialogue together.
'Hello, I am here for my pay.' Denis uses a polite everyday Russian courtesy expression that sets the tone of the conversation right away.
'Today is the big match.' In everyday Russian, 'today' flows straight into 'game' without extra linking words.
'Are you a Spartak fan too?' Denis uses the polite plural form of address to maintain a respectful or ironic distance.
'I am a gladiator. Sit down.' Notice how Russian puts 'sit' and 'sit down' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
Завтра я тебе спартаковский бар покажу.
'Tomorrow I will show you a great Spartak bar.' Here Chef Barinov anchors the thought on 'tomorrow' and finishes on 'will show', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
'I can't, I have to look for a job.' In everyday Russian, 'can, am able to' flows straight into 'to look for' without extra linking words.
'Alright, it was nice meeting you.' Denis pairs 'pleasant' with 'to get acquainted, to meet' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
Виктор Петрович, я могу что-нибудь для вас сделать напоследок?

'Viktor Petrovich, can I do anything for you as a parting favor?' Notice how Russian puts 'can, am able to' and 'favor' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
'You can. Take that young guy back.' Here Chef Barinov anchors the thought on 'can' and finishes on 'back, the other way', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
'That is my final request.' In everyday Russian, 'last, final' flows straight into 'a request' without extra linking words.
'Alright, I will.' Lyova centers this short reply on 'good, well, all right', letting a few direct words carry the whole meaning.

'Never give up.' Notice how Russian puts 'never' and 'give up' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect. Let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Завтра я тебе спартаковский бар покажу.
Виктор Петрович, я могу что-нибудь для вас сделать напоследок?
And that brings Episode Two of Season Four to a dramatic finish as Viktor gets Denis rehired and accidentally strikes Nagiyev in the rain. See you in the next episode. See you next time!
